QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_18

question.text: 'Lotus Category II AIF' has negotiated AFFIRMATIVE rights in a start-up investee. Which of the following BEST describes an affirmative right?

answer.text: A corporate action that CANNOT be carried out without the AIF's express consent, even if an ordinary majority of 51% shareholders approves it
A right to receive first claim on exit proceeds
A right to convert debentures to equity at par value
A right to appoint the Managing Director

explanation.text: The Logic: Affirmative rights are 'positive control' — even if a matter could pass with ordinary resolution (51% simple majority), the action CANNOT be effected without the affirmative-right holder's express consent. They cover items like capital structure changes, MOA/AOA alteration, new debt, IPO decisions, M&A, ESOP changes, etc. The Trap: First claim on exit = liquidation preference. MD appointment = board/governance right, not affirmative right per se. Debenture conversion terms = hybrid security terms. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests affirmative rights identically. Veto rights are the 'mirror' — affirmative needs YES consent; veto gives the power to say NO. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep the affirmative-rights list 'exhaustive not illustrative' in drafting — courts in India have declined to add implied affirmative rights. If a matter isn't listed, the AIF loses the veto.
